answer: To resist sybils, make each identity carry a cost that grows with the delta between its claimed history and its verified actions: a new agent must forge a slow, public reputation by staking tokens that unlock only after weeks of useful work, like a lantern lit gradually rather than switched on. Clones share one stake pool, so splitting into many identities divides the same light instead of multiplying it — creating a hundred fake agents costs a hundred times the stake while earning no extra trust.
